title: Clearance Manifest v0.2
description: Additive v0.2 of the Clearance Manifest. The entire v0.1 body is carried unchanged (v0.1 is frozen; no published v0.1 URI moves), plus three new OPTIONAL top-level axes: `grantAuthority` (does the declaring party HOLD the right they purport to grant — gates a clearance facet CLOSED when a right has been assigned away), `designation` (what the work may lawfully be CALLED and who may call it that — MUST NEVER touch any clearance facet), and `evidence` (tamper-evident pointers to off-manifest evidence a HUMAN judges — never changes any verdict). Every substantive claim in the new axes is a DECLARED self-claim: OpenClearance records and points; it does not adjudicate, verify, or grade. Cross-field consistency rules (the authority gate, the designation/evidence input bans, evidence-pointer resolution, the protected-name guard) are verifier-enforced, not schema-expressible; a manifest violating them is inconsistent and a conforming verifier MUST treat it as REJECTED. v0.1-safe bridge: a v0.1 manifest MAY carry these three blocks inside `extensions` under the key 'https://openclearance.org/v0.2/'; a v0.1 consumer MUST-ignores them, and whenever `grantAuthority` gates a facet closed the v0.1-visible clearance boolean itself MUST already read false, so a v0.1-only consumer still reads the safe answer.

@context.description: JSON-LD context. MUST include the openclearance v0.2 context IRI: the sole normative authority for expansion and validation. Terms carried from v0.1 keep their v0.1 vocabulary IRIs; only new v0.2 terms mint in the v0.2 vocabulary.

specVersion.description: Human-readable version convenience. Not normative: the @context IRI fixes the actual vocabulary.

work.description: The work being cleared. Only `id` is guaranteed; descriptive fields are present on the accept path and absent on the deny path (a rejected record is not fully identified).

lifespan.description: Display-form life dates (e.g. '1853-1890'); not a structured date.

source.description: Provenance source. `museum` is guaranteed (its `code` is the federation identifier); URLs and images are present on the accept path.

rights.description: The rights determination carried (not adjudicated) by this manifest.

statement.description: Rights-statement URI (CC / rightsstatements.org). null on a deny: no positive open-rights statement applies.

sourceApiValue.description: Forensic link binding the raw museum API value to its field name. null on a deny.

clearance.description: The instant, machine-actionable answer. Each facet pairs a boolean with a structured basis. NORMATIVE: no facet's basis.inputs may reference any designation or evidence path — designation never restricts reproduction, and evidence never changes a verdict; a manifest doing either is inconsistent and MUST be rejected by a conforming verifier.

verification.description: How the rights determination was reached, as an auditable event. Actor vs tool are distinct; on a deny the actor is the engine rights-gate, not the museum.

citation.description: Rendered attribution strings. Omitted for an unidentified rejected record.

grantAuthority.description: AUTHORITY axis: who holds the authority to grant reuse of this work. Orthogonal to `clearance` (which records permission). Declared, never looked up. v0.2 carries only `collectingSociety`; the block is named so a future publisher / estate / gallery-exclusive assignment slots beside it without a schema break. Absent = no authority declaration: for an artist-signed record that reads as unknown (fail-closed on reproduction); for an open-access CC0/public-domain record the block is simply not applicable — the CC0/PD basis already grounds the grant, and a collecting society cannot re-encumber a public-domain work. NORMATIVE (verifier-enforced): when `assignedCategories` contains 'commercial-reproduction' or 'reproduction-all', the v0.1-visible clearance.commercialReproduction.permitted MUST read false (rule 'right-assigned-to-collecting-society'); 'derivative' gates clearance.derivatives symmetrically; 'unknown' fails commercial reproduction closed. A manifest asserting a facet true alongside such an assignment is inconsistent and MUST be REJECTED.

society.description: Registered collecting society the artist belongs to, or 'none'. 'other' + `societyName` for a society outside the v0.2 baseline set.

societyName.description: Free-text society name. REQUIRED when society='other'; schema-enforced below.

memberId.description: The artist's membership identifier if held; null if unknown/not provided. Never required — many members do not know their ID.

assignedCategories.description: THE substantive item: which rights categories the artist assigned to the society. Determines whether a `clearance` facet is the artist's to grant. Open, honesty-bearing set. 'none' = member but nothing relevant assigned (artist retains all); 'unknown' = member, assignment scope not yet confirmed, which fails reproduction closed. 'none' and 'unknown' are SENTINELS, not categories: each MUST be the array's only member when present (schema-enforced) — a manifest cannot simultaneously claim 'nothing assigned' and name a specific assigned category, or claim both 'nothing assigned' and 'not yet confirmed'.

verification.description: How the declaration may be checked, and by whom it has been — PROVENANCE for the declaration, never a second verdict. MANUAL link-out only: no automated registry call is made or implied (no complete registry API exists, and an automated name-search yields false negatives, which fail-open — the exact wrong direction). If a human checking `registryUrl` finds the assignment differs from what was declared, they correct `assignedCategories` itself — the authority gate reads only `assignedCategories`, never this block, so there is no separate 'verified' or 'conflict' state for OpenClearance to assert.

registryUrl.description: The society's public name-search / member page a human uses to check. A pointer, not a data source OpenClearance reads.

verifiedBy.description: Who performed a manual check against `registryUrl`, if any. Absent = declared and never checked; presence records that someone looked, not that OpenClearance vouches for the result.

verifiedAt.description: When the check happened, if it did.

designation.description: DESIGNATION axis: what this work may lawfully be CALLED, and who is entitled to call it that. Orthogonal to `clearance` (permission) and `grantAuthority` (authority-to-grant). NORMATIVE: this block MUST NOT restrict any `clearance` facet — a protected designation constrains what a NEW PRODUCT may be NAMED, never whether an existing work may be REPRODUCED; a CC0/public-domain work carrying a designation mark remains fully cleared for reproduction. Every claim here is SELF-ATTESTED: OpenClearance records it and does not verify it. Absence of this block is not a finding either way — it means only that no claim was declared, never that no cultural rights exist.

marks.description: Protected origin/authenticity marks CLAIMED for this work. Empty = none claimed — which is NOT an assertion that none apply, and NOT a negative finding.

evidence.description: GENERAL evidence-pointer block: tamper-evident POINTERS to evidence held OFF-MANIFEST. OpenClearance hosts no bytes. NORMATIVE: evidence NEVER changes a verdict — no basis.inputs may cite an evidence item, and attaching evidence never moves a manifest up the tier ladder; OpenClearance records and points, it does not adjudicate or grade. Evidence exists so a HUMAN can judge. Empty/absent = no evidence offered, which is NOT a negative finding.

extensions.description: Forward-compatible vendor escape hatch. Producers MAY carry namespaced extension data here; consumers MUST ignore terms they do not recognise.

basis.description: The structured reasoning behind one clearance boolean. Shape is normative; rule ids are an open set (see the rule registry).

rule.description: Bare kebab-case determination-rule id resolving to https://openclearance.org/v0.2/rules#<rule>. NOT a closed enum: an unrecognised id is valid and yields an 'unrecognised_rule' advisory.

protectedMark.description: A CLAIMED protected mark. SELF-ATTESTED throughout. OpenClearance carries the claim and points at any evidence the claimant offers (via the `evidence` block); it does NOT verify, grade, or adjudicate it. Note what is NOT here: no verification block, no register adjudication, no verified state — a mark carrying any such field is schema-invalid by construction.

schemeName.description: e.g. 'GI Registry (India)', 'Toi Iho', 'Igloo Tag', 'Indigenous Art Code'. REQUIRED when scheme='other'; schema-enforced below.

legalBasis.description: The ACTUAL legal force of the mark being claimed. Honesty-bearing: a VOLUNTARY CODE (a dealer code of conduct) MUST NOT be recorded as though it conferred a statutory designation right.

name.description: The protected designation claimed, e.g. 'Orissa Pattachitra'.

designationRef.description: OPTIONAL reference identifying WHICH designation is meant (disambiguation only — 'Pattachitra' is ambiguous without it). NORMATIVE: this identifies the DESIGNATION, never the CLAIMANT. It confers ZERO verification and MUST NOT be presented as evidence that this work or maker qualifies.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the granting jurisdiction ('IN','NZ','CA','AU') or 'EU'. A designation right is TERRITORIAL — it does not travel.

workDesignation.description: Does the CLAIMANT assert the work is of this protected class? DESCRIPTIVE, self-attested. Carries NO reproduction restriction. A hedged 'attributed' claim resolves like 'unknown' for product naming: the protected name is withheld (rule 'designation-claim-attributed-only').

producerClaim.description: The maker's SELF-ATTESTED entitlement claim. OpenClearance records only what the claimant states. It MUST NOT record a third-party NEGATIVE finding ('not authorised') — it has no adjudication path to ground one, and a false negative would defame an honest maker.

claimsAuthorisation.description: 'claimed' = the maker asserts authorised-user / licensee status. 'not-claimed' = they make no such claim (NOT a finding that they are unauthorised). 'not-applicable' = the maker predates or falls outside the scheme (e.g. an 18th-century artisan).

authorisedUserRef.description: A membership/authorised-user identifier the maker CHOOSES to state. Self-attested. OpenClearance does not look it up. Its presence changes NO verdict.

declaredBy.description: WHO made this claim, in PROV terms. The claim is THEIRS, accountably — that is the whole trust model. Not OpenClearance's finding.

productNaming.description: The instant, machine-actionable answer for a product DERIVED from this work: may that product be DESIGNATED by the protected name? Reuses the v0.1 basis shape. This is the ONLY thing the designation axis gates — it NEVER gates reproduction. It is a deterministic function of the DECLARED inputs, not an adjudication of their truth. NORMATIVE (verifier-enforced): `true` requires a mark whose workDesignation and producerClaim.claimsAuthorisation are both 'claimed' AND whose legalBasis is a confirmed basis (statutory-gi / certification-trademark / collective-trademark — never voluntary-code, never unknown); the basis.summary MUST state that the verdict rests on the declarant's own attestation and is not verified by OpenClearance. basis.inputs MUST NOT cite an evidence item — evidence never upgrades this verdict.

protectedNameUsePermitted.description: MAY a derived product be designated BY the protected name, ON THE STRENGTH OF THE DECLARANT'S OWN ATTESTATION, IN `jurisdiction`? `false` does not forbid truthfully DESCRIBING the work and does not restrict reproduction — withholding the name is not an accusation, and 'not-claimed' is never rendered as 'not authorised'.

permittedDescriptor.description: The honest phrasing a product MAY lawfully bear, e.g. 'Fine-art print reproducing a Pattachitra painting (Odisha, 18th century), after the original held by the museum'.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this verdict is scoped to (matches the relevant marks[].jurisdiction). A designation right is territorial: a consumer operating outside this jurisdiction MUST NOT read `protectedNameUsePermitted` as applying there. `true` in one jurisdiction says nothing about any other; fail-closed on the name outside scope.

evidenceItem.description: One tamper-evident pointer to off-manifest evidence. No grade, score, rank, sufficiency test, or authenticity finding exists here, and none may be added — whether the evidence is convincing is a human's judgment, and OpenClearance has no opinion.

id.description: Stable id, unique within the manifest.

type.description: The KIND of evidence. Descriptive only — it carries no weight and implies no grade.

typeName.description: Free-text kind. REQUIRED when type='other'; schema-enforced below.

supports.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the CLAIM this evidence is offered in support of, e.g. '/designation/marks/0' or '/grantAuthority/collectingSociety'. Any self-attested claim may be pointed at. One direction only: a claim never lists its evidence, so the two can never disagree. NORMATIVE (verifier-enforced): the pointer MUST resolve to a node that exists in the manifest; an evidence item silently pointing at nothing makes the manifest invalid.

mediaType.description: IANA media type of the evidence bytes, e.g. 'video/mp4', 'image/jpeg'.

integrity.description: SHA-256 over the exact bytes of the evidence. THE tamper-evident binding: content-addressed, so the evidence cannot be swapped. Same idiom as the v0.1 Tier-0 envelope.

locator.description: Where the bytes may be fetched. OpenClearance hosts NONE of this. The hash is the identity; locators are convenience/mirrors. A dead locator does NOT invalidate the manifest and changes no verdict.

capturedAt.description: SELF-ASSERTED capture time. Protected from ALTERATION by the manifest's integrity protection, but NOT anchored to an independent clock. Absent an RFC-3161 token this does NOT prove the evidence was not backdated, and the manifest MUST NOT claim independent timestamping without one.

declaredBy.description: Who offers this evidence, in PROV terms. The evidence is THEIR attestation, not OpenClearance's finding.

caption.description: Human-readable caption for display by a hosting platform. Descriptive; carries no weight.

timeAnchor.description: OPTIONAL independent time anchor over `integrity.hash`. FORWARD-COMPATIBLE: RFC-3161 is DEFINED here but is NOT yet live in the reference implementation. When type='none' or the anchor is absent, the evidence time is SELF-ASSERTED and the manifest MUST NOT claim independent timestamping or non-backdating.

token.description: base64 DER RFC-3161 TimeStampToken over integrity.hash. Present only when type='rfc3161'.

tsa.description: The third-party Time Stamping Authority that issued the token.
